newsitem.title: USA: Falcon Drilling upbeat on 1997 prospects.
newsitem.headline: Falcon Drilling upbeat on 1997 prospects.

text.p: Falcon Drilling Co Inc said it had its third consecutive quarter of record results in the first quarter ended in March and its management believes earnings momentum should continue through 1997.
The company said it bases its positive outlook for utilization and day rates in its domestic segments and planned capacity additions.
In particular, it said results in the second quarter will benefit from five factors.

These include a higher number of available rigs than in the first quarter due to upgrades, the addition April 11 of its 26th active deep barge rig, an early return to service of its drillship, Peregrine III and a new one, Peregrine I.
It said the quarter would see the first full quarter's impact of its newly acquired inland marine service business.
"Our outlook remains very positive," Steven Webster, Falcon's chairman and chief executive said. "Falcon continues to capitalize on the positive operating leverage inherent in its fleet," he said.
"Falcon's actively marketed fleet remains fully committed and dayrates are increasing in this tight market environment," Webster added.
Late Wednesday, the company reported earnings for the first quarter of 1997 of $17.0 million, or $0.43 per share, versus $995,000, or $0.03 per share, in first quarter 1996.
First quarter revenues were $109.9 million versus $56.1 million in the same period a year ago.
